exploration.title: Pollinator Express
exploration.subject: Biology
exploration.summary: Guide a bee between flowers and test when a visit transfers compatible pollen.
exploration.question: Is visiting any flower enough to pollinate it?
exploration.explanation: Pollination moves pollen to the receptive part of a flower and can allow seeds to develop. Animals may carry pollen while gathering food. In this model, a bee transfers pollen only between different flowers of the same species. Added habitat flowers can help it cross a gap. The bee carries pollen from only its last visit; flight limits and flower types are invented. Real pollination can involve mixed pollen, self-pollination, wind and other animals, and does not always result in seeds.

experiments.title: A visit or a transfer?
experiments.instruction: Predict which visit will transfer compatible pollen. Visit Gold 1, then Gold 2. Reset and compare Gold 1 followed by Violet 1.
experiments.observe: Compare visits with compatible transfers. Explain why two visits do not necessarily mean two pollinated flowers.

experiments.title: Bridge a habitat gap
experiments.instruction: Set flight reach to 170 and leave habitat patches off. Visit Gold 1 and Gold 2, then predict whether Gold 3 is reachable. Reset, add habitat patches and repeat the route via Gold bridge.
experiments.observe: Compare the possible paths before and after adding flowers. Explain how an extra feeding stop can connect otherwise separated patches in this model.

exploration.misconception: Bees are not the only pollinators, and a flower visit is not a guarantee of fertilization or seed production.
